runs.name: MDU Resources Group, Inc.; NYSE MDU, SEC CIK 0000067716, Delaware; regulated electric in North Dakota, Montana, South Dakota and Wyoming, natural gas distribution in eight states and the WBI interstate pipeline; Knife River separated 2023-05-31, Everus 2024-10-31
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: Price **$19.00** (close 2026-10-16, `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares 210,349,456 common on the cover of the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (0000067716-26-000072, as of 2026-07-30), `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing, no treasury stock; beside the count, forward sale agreements of the December 2025 offering for about 7.4 million shares and $139.6M, unsettled. Sovereign **5.43%**, the US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (`tools/sources.py`, issuing authority). Read from the 10-K for FY2025 (0000067716-26-000014), the 10-Q to 2026-06-30, the proxy of 2026-04-01 (0000067716-26-000040), the 8-K releases, the 10-Ks for FY2019, FY2022, FY2023 and FY2024 and Everus's Form 10/A of 2024-10-09. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. Window FY2021 to FY2025 on continuing operations after the Knife River (2023-05-31) and Everus (2024-10-31) separations; FY2021 built as a CONVENTION of the run, the FY2023 10-K's continuing operations less Everus's own Form 10 figures, tested on FY2022 (capital spending and depreciation exact, operating cash 3.6% high). **Q1 IN**: three rate-regulated monopolies, Montana-Dakota electric, gas distribution in eight states (Montana-Dakota, Cascade, Intermountain) and the WBI interstate pipeline. **Q2 IN**: gas distribution decides at 37.8% of 2021 to 2025 operating income (electric 32.8%, pipeline 29.3%); a franchised local monopoly at regulator-set ordinary returns (allowed returns on equity 9.5% to 9.65% in the 2025 cases), carried to Q3 as a second best; narrowing slowly in Washington and Oregon, 43% of gas retail revenue, on the building code limiting gas and the pending litigation, the stricter reading recorded. **Q3 weighs against**: capital spending 2.3 to 3.7 times depreciation; 5.1% on capital employed and 7.0% on equity against 9.5% allowed; about 6.5% cash return on added capital. **Q4 accounts IN, weighs against, no STOP**: ten balance sheets read through the two separations (retained earnings down $970M and $400M at the distributions), goodwill $346M all in gas distribution, borrowings $2.58bn about 49% of debt plus equity; the earnings-guidance habit carried to Q5; depreciation probably short of real maintenance. **Q5 integrity IN, ability weighs against**: Intermountain breached its interest-coverage covenant at 2025-09-30, cross-defaulting MDU Energy Capital's notes and the credit lines until waived, told plainly in the 10-K; earned returns well below allowed. **Q6 weighs against on both parts**: a 60 to 70% payout dividend paid while selling shares (an 11.7M-share forward sale at $19.70 and an at-the-market programme), no buybacks since the separations, Bakken East at $2.7bn to $3.2bn undecided; pay on adjusted EPS with no capital charge. **Q7 OUT on the floor**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 negative every year after all spending (mean -$206.0M), $144.6M after depreciation, $219.2M before interest all-equity; not a serial acquirer (the 49% Badger Wind interest, $264.6M in December 2025, deducted inside capital spending), so the default pair is central and no organic-pair figure is reported; floor tested first, expected return at the price 3.36% no growth and 4.31% shown growth all-equity, 5.15% on a deliberately generous case. Value range $7.16 to $9.70 a share all-equity at the sovereign (equity-only $9.60 to $12.66), the price about twice the top; fair price -$3.39 all-equity, not positive (both ends at ten percent worth less than $2,530.9M of net debt), $3.86 equity-only. The 10-K names no SEC-filing rival; BKH, NWE and AVA chosen from the proxy's peer groups as a CONVENTION of the run: 2017 to 2025 average return on equity 9.4%, 8.3% and 7.5%, return on assets 2.88%, 2.85% and 2.36%, MDU's three utility segments 2.62% on assets, its gas segment 1.46% in 2017 and 1.43% in 2025, the weakest of the group. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` directory listing showing the HOKCY and XNGSY runs of today, HOKCY commit subjects in the opening git status, AYI and ARCB folder names and a memory index line; none used. Commits c7ad2740 (template), 790e48de (Step 0 and Q1), a3778194 (Q2), dca66b13 (Q3), 70694cea (Q4), 32bf20e5 (Q5), 04a62d28 (Q6), 927af863 (Q7 with the buyback line written back), da309836 (the rest). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` 74 ids, no E-ids, 64 quoted fragments beside an id, 0 slips; **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): a five-year window across two separations with no filing restating the first year; a deciding part earning well below its regulator's allowed return; state policy as the threat to a deciding part; whether depreciation counts as the maintenance guess under (e), and the growth case inverting between the sovereign and ten percent; the tax rate of the all-equity interest add-back; a negative fair price and what alert it sets; forward sale agreements in the share count and net debt; comparators when the 10-K names none. Not armed: the all-equity fair is not positive and the run reports no organic-pair figure (not a serial acquirer); the equity-only $3.86 alert is left to the operator. Could not get: a filing restating FY2021 for both separations, a maintenance and growth split of capital spending, earned returns by state, Intermountain's own coverage.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7, on the floor (MDU Resources Group, NYSE MDU, regulated electric, gas distribution and pipeline after the Knife River and Everus separations; Q1 IN; Q2 IN, gas distribution decides at 37.8%, a franchise at regulator-set ordinary returns carried as a second best, narrowing slowly in Washington and Oregon; Q3, Q4 and Q6 against: spending 2.3 to 3.7 times depreciation, 7.0% on equity against 9.5% allowed, owner cash negative after all spending every year, shares sold to fund a ratio dividend; Q5 integrity IN, ability against on the Intermountain covenant breach. Best expected return 4.31% all-equity at $19.00; value range $7.16 to $9.70 a share at the 5.43% Treasury rate; fair price -$3.39 all-equity, not positive, $3.86 equity-only; not armed, the equity-only alert left to the operator. No citation slip. Framework gaps for the operator: a window across two separations, earned below allowed returns, state policy at Q2, depreciation as the maintenance guess, a negative fair price, forward sale shares.)
